question.leadin: Give the following about the Non-Aligned Movement, an organization of countries interested in protecting their interests against both the Soviet-dominated Warsaw Pact and the US-dominated NATO.
question.text: The Non-Aligned Movement grew out of the Bandung Conference, a 1955 meeting hosted by President Sukarno on this country's island of Java.
question.clue: The disgraced bishop Carlos Ximenes Belo reported on a massacre perpetrated by this country in the Santa Cruz cemetery.

swap.leadin: The American evacuation from this country was signaled by the playing of Irving Berlin's "White Christmas" on the radio in April.
swap.text: Name this country where helicopters extracted over 2,000 people in Operation Frequent Wind in 1975, marking the end of American involvement in a Southeast Asian war.
swap.clue: Gia Long was the first emperor of its last ruling dynasty, and during the early 20th century, this country adopted the Quoc Ngu writing system.

question.leadin: This woman won the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize but could not accept it in person, as the ruling military junta held her under house arrest.
question.text: Name this activist and politician who became State Counsellor of her country in 2016. Since her rise to power, she has been heavily criticized for her inaction against the persecution of the Rohingya people.
question.answerHtml: Aung San Suu Kyi ([ong sahn soo chee], but be lenient) (prompt on “Suu” or “Kyi” alone)
question.clue: She leads the National League for Democracy, which she formed after the 8888 Uprising to protest against General Ne Win's dictatorship.

swap.text: The victims of the Kent State shooting were protesting the bombing of Cambodia during this war. Boxer Muhammad Ali was jailed for refusing to be drafted to fight in this war.
swap.clue: A "trail" was bombed in this war's Operation Rolling Thunder, and Agent Orange was sprayed on forests during it.

question.text: This man commanded the Philippine Revolutionary Army against the Spanish during the Spanish-American War, only to turn against the US during the Philippine-American War. He became the first President of the Philippines in 1897.
question.clue: Earlier, he quarreled with Andres Bonifacio over divisions in the Katipunan movement.

swap.text: This city's namesake galleons made trips to the New World to exchange gold for Ming goods. This city's bay was the site of a Spanish-American War battle in which George Dewey defeated the Spanish fleet.
swap.clue: Andres de Urdaneta discovered a route east from this city, which received silver from Potosi and Acapulco as the center of Spain's Pacific trade empire aboard namesake "Galleons."

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about 20th century Asian dictators.
question.text: This leader of the Khmer Rouge ruled as dictator of Cambodia between 1976 and 1979. His agrarian socialist policies and political purges killed over a million of his own people.
question.clue: This leader, who was referred to as "Brother Number One", helped Prince Sihanouk's ("SEE-uh-nook") attempt to return to power after he was deposed in a coup by Lon Nol.

swap.text: The Ayutthaya controlled land in this modern-day country. European traders who initially encountered the Ayutthaya called this country Siam.
swap.clue: Its rulers used the Paknam Incident to create an irredentist nationalism later deployed by the Phibun government.

question.text: The Vietnamese invasion of Cambodia also allowed this communist movement in a neighboring country to establish a namesake "People's Democratic Republic" in 1975.
question.clue: The book Man in the Region of Death was an account of this organization's prison camps by former RLG official Thongthip Rathanavilai, though unlike the Khmer Rouge this organization never established massive death camps.

swap.text: This Filipino ethnic group, which specialized in creating vinta, was known for piracy in the Sulu Sea. This Islamic group sought to create an independent state in Mindanao.
swap.clue: The defeat of these people acting as pirates led James Brooke to be crowned White Rajah.

question.leadin: Sufi merchants may have brought Islam to this modern day country while traveling across the Indian Ocean.
question.text: Name this modern-day country whose Hindu state collapsed after the Demak Sultanate took control of Java.
question.clue: The "Guided Democracy" system was pursued by this country's first president, Sukarno, before he was overthrown by Suharto.

swap.leadin: This party forced urban "New People" to move to the countryside and become "Old People"
swap.text: Name this political party which lost power after an invasion by the Vietnamese in 1979. It was responsible for the murder of thousands of prisoners in its country's "Killing Fields".
swap.clue: This regime, which was defeated by the Salvation Front, gained popular support after Operations Menu and Freedom Deal.

question.leadin: Antonio da Madalena is credited with being the first Western visitor to this location.
question.text: Name this location that Henri Mouhot supposedly "discovered" despite it being known to natives for centuries. The "customs" of this location were written about by Zhou Daguan.
question.answerHtml: Angkor [accept Angkor Wat; accept Angkor Thom; prompt on Khmer Empire; prompt on but do not reveal Cambodia]
question.clue: It served as the capital for a dynasty led by Jayavarman and Suryavarman, and it sits on the Siam Reap River.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Hindu kingdoms outside the Indian subcontinent.
swap.text: This kingdom in modern-day Vietnam was surrounded by the Khmer empire and Đai Viet until it was annexed in 1471 by Vietnamese emperor Le Nhan Tong. This kingdom's king Bhadravarman I built the My Son ("mee sun") temple complex.
swap.clue: Upon conquering the neighbouring Funan Kingdom, Shaivism became the state religion, and the kingdom was involved in the Spice Route as a producer of aloe.

question.leadin: Some of the most vicious combat in this campaign was seen during the engagement known as the Battle of the Tennis Court.
question.text: Name this theatre of the Second World War where Operation U-Go was halted in two fierce battles in 1944 when infiltration tactics and encirclement were rendered ineffective by air supply to the defenders, while many of the attacking force's 50,000-plus casualties were caused by malnutrition and malaria.

swap.text: Much earlier, Laos's capital at Vientiane had been sacked by this "great" king of Thailand in 1775. This only member of the Thonburi dynasty defeated the Burmese invaders that had destroyed Ayutthaya and was executed by a general who took the throne as Rama I.
swap.answerHtml: Taksin the Great [or Somdet Phra Chao Taksin Maha Rat]
swap.clue: This ruler stabilized the frontier by conquering the Lanna kingdom after leading a guerilla war to repel an occupation by the Konbaung ("kohn-baong") dynasty of Burma.

question.leadin: The Jiaqing Emperor agreed for a new tributary state to adopt this name after reversing the order of its two words to avoid association with the ancient state of Nanyue.
question.text: The first part of what place name came after Đai, or "Great," from the 15th to 18th century? From 1839 to 1945, the second part of this place name also followed Đai.

swap.text: With tacit approval from US ambassador Henry Cabot Lodge Jr., this man led a group of generals that overthrew and assassinated Diem in 1963. He later surrendered to communist forces in 1975 as South Vietnam's last president.

question.text: This city was the original location of the Kamthieng House, which was a traditional home typical of the Lanna Kingdom, of which it was the capital for about five hundred years. It also names one of the successors to the Lanna Kingdom.

swap.text: Along with the islands in the Labuan territory, East Malaysia is made up of these two states found on the north of the island of Borneo.
swap.answerHtml: Sabah and Sarawak [order not important but don't accept or prompt on just one]
